Anand Bansal: Good afternoon, everyone. I'm Anand Bansal, joined by my colleague Vineet 
Ranjan. Thank you for joining us. We'll wait for a couple of minutes to allow more participants 
to log in. 
 
Vineet, we currently have 100 participants with us. Over to you to get us started. 
 
Vineet Ranjan: Thank you, Anand. Good evening, everyone. Welcome to InfoEdge India 
Limited Q2 FY27 earnings conference call. Joining us today from the management, we have 
Mr. Sanjeev Bikhchandani, Founder and Vice Chairman, Mr. Hitesh Oberoi, Co-Promoter and 
Managing Director, and Mr. Himanshu Agarwal, Chief Financial Officer. Before we begin, I 
would like to draw your attention to the detailed disclaimer included in the presentation for 
good order's sake. Kindly note that this conference call is being recorded and all participant 
lines will be on mute, and there'll be an opportunity for Q&A towards the end of the call. 
 
Now I'll hand over the call to Hitesh for his opening remarks. Thank you, and over to you, 
Hitesh. 
 
Hitesh Oberoi: Thank you, Vineet, and a very good evening to everyone. Thank you for joining 
InfoEdge's earnings call for the second quarter and first half of FY27. I will start with our 
overall read for the quarter and the half year and then take you through each business in 
more detail. 
 
In Q2, standalone billings grew 13% YoY. Revenue grew 13% to Rs.842 crores and operating 
profit grew 30% to Rs.347 crores. The operating PBT margin was 41%, up 541 basis points 
year on year. Cash generated from operations was Rs.373 crores, up 27%. 
 
For the first half, billings grew 14%, revenue grew 12% and operating profit grew 32%. Cash 
generated from operations in H1 was Rs.598 crores, up 27%, and we ended September with 
a cash balance of Rs.4,976 crores. The detailed numbers are in the earnings deck. 
 
Recruitment, 99acres and Jeevansathi together are growing faster than the standalone 
numbers suggest, while reported growth is diluted by Shiksha, which is undergoing a 
structural transition. Excluding Shiksha, standalone billings grew over 14% in Q2 and about 
16% in H1, against reported growth of 13% and 14%, respectively. 
 
Starting with the Recruitment segment, in Q2, Recruitment billings grew 13% and revenue 
grew 13%. Operating profit increased 20% at an operating PBT margin of 59%, and cash from 
operations increased by 20%. As we indicated in our billing update earlier this month, the 
timing of customer renewals affected reported growth this quarter. Some clients renew 
ahead of schedule while others defer to a later quarter, shifting billings between quarters 
without changing the underlying trend. 
 
In Q1, timing lifted reported growth to 17.5%. In Q2, it worked in the opposite direction. 
Adjusting for these timing differences, we estimate underlying growth at around 15% in Q1 
and around 14% to 15% in Q2. For this reason, we believe the half-year performance provides 
a more reliable read than any single quarter. H1 Recruitment billings grew 15%, and over a 
longer period, these timing differences partly even out. 
 

In our core India B2B recruitment business, the drivers are broadly similar to Q1. Hiring 
activity stayed steady, led mainly by replacement demand, with some pickup in a few 
segments. Enterprise renewal rates held up and premium hiring continued to do better than 
the broader market. Across sectors, Q2 billings grew 3% in IT, Tech and BPM, 7% for GCCs and 
18% in other sectors, while recruitment consultant billings grew 7%. As renewal timing 
affected these numbers as well, the half year gives a relatively better picture. In H1, growth 
was 9% in IT, Tech and BPM, 19% in GCCs, 16% in other sectors and 5% for consultants. Other 
sectors' growth improved in H1 over last year, led mainly by BFSI, Consumer, Retail and 
Manufacturing sectors. 
 
Beyond B2B, our jobseeker business, Naukri 360, grew billings by 37%. Paid subscribers are 
now 2.7% of monthly active users, compared with 1.3% in January'25. AI-led services are 
playing a growing role in conversion. The business operated at an operating PBT margin of 
64%. Job Hai, while still small, grew billings by 86%, with investment levels broadly 
unchanged. Lastly, NaukriGulf grew by 9%. It remains profitable at margins of around 36%, 
and we see scope for growth to recover as and when conditions in the region normalize. 
 
AI and data products billings now contribute a high single-digit share of our Recruitment 
topline, with an annualized run rate of around Rs.240 crores based on Q2. This comes from 
AI-Rex and Talent Pulse on the B2B side, and from AI-led services for jobseekers such as mock 
interviews, our jobseeker agent Neo and the AI resume making service. 
 
Enterprise uptake normally follows a familiar path. Customers first try the product. They start 
small, embed it in their hiring workflows, and then commit larger budgets. Early feedback on 
both AI-Rex and Talent Pulse has been very positive. Our focus now is to add customers, 
deepen usage and show measurable value, so that consumption grows materially over time. 
 
Building an AI product is getting easier. Getting it adopted at scale is not. We work with over 
150,000 paying recruiter clients through a sales network across 80+ cities, and our platform 
with 120 million profiles, with around 20,000 added and over 9 lakh updated every day. This 
combination of distribution, data and jobseeker scale is difficult to replicate, and we believe 
it gives us a clear right to win in AI-led hiring. 
 
At its core, Naukri is a sourcing platform. Recruiters search our resume database to find and 
reach the right candidates, complemented by job postings. Hiring volumes follow the macro 
environment, so our effort is focused on what we can influence: our share of hiring and what 
we earn per hire. We are doing this by building a broader set of hiring solutions around the 
core, including AI-led sourcing, talent intelligence, employer branding, assisted hiring and 
assessments, across the premium, mid-market and value segments. 
 
In the premium segment, which includes Naukri Top Tier, PremiumX, iimjobs and Hirist, 
several capabilities are packaged at no extra cost today, leaving room for further 
monetization. In the mid-market, the focus is recruiter productivity and adjacent services, 
while in the value segment, Job Hai is building an AI-enabled marketplace for SMEs and 
enterprises hiring full-time and gig workers, and recruitment firms. For jobseekers, we are 
adding career insights, upskilling and interview preparation through Naukri 360, Minis and 
Coding Ninjas. These are largely self-serve and margin accretive. 
 

Moving over to the Real Estate segment, growth in 99acres continues to accelerate. Billings 
grew by 21% YoY in Q2, up from 17% in Q1. Revenue grew 17%. Operating losses reduced 
significantly by 93% from Rs.23 crores in Q2FY26 to less than Rs.2 crores in Q2 FY27. 99acres 
generated cash from operations of Rs.22 crores in Q2, against Rs.2 crores a year ago. 
 
Our leadership position strengthened further across key operating metrics. Web time share 
amongst the top three portals was 49% in Q2 and 51% in September. App time share was 49% 
in Q2 and 50% in September, up from 27% in Q2 of last year, based on SimilarWeb's revised 
app data series. App DAUs grew 25% YoY. 
 
Supply momentum remained healthy across categories. Live listings across resale, rental and 
commercial grew 23% YoY from owners and 14% from brokers, while new project listings 
grew 15%. More brokers, developers and owners are choosing 99acres to market residential 
and commercial properties across the country. 
 
Traffic leadership, wider supply and product improvements are translating into higher 
engagement. Property enquiries across all categories put together grew 33% YoY. We also 
continue to optimize our marketing mix and get more out of our marketing spend. Marketing 
investment was about 13% lower YoY, while enquiries kept growing. This demonstrates how 
market leadership can begin to translate into better economics. We continue to apply AI 
across user experience, enquiry generation, marketing and operations, with early benefits 
visible in engagement and marketing efficiency improvements. 
 
Looking ahead, we aim to gain further share in H2, in both traffic and revenue, and will 
continue to invest to support this while improving profitability at the same time. New Projects 
remain a significant opportunity, which we estimate at about Rs.6,000 crores across digital 
and non-digital spend. Expanding our presence here is a strategic priority, through 
investments in content, product and client delivery. We are also taking 99Shorts beyond NCR 
to more cities. As our lead over other portals widens across supply, traffic and monetization, 
we expect operating leverage to emerge progressively through the rest of FY27. We expect 
99acres to generate positive operating cash for FY27, with cash generation strengthening over 
time. 
 
Moving over to the Matchmaking segment. Matchmaking billings grew 23% in Q2, with 
Jeevansathi up 18% and Aisle up 40%. The segment operated near breakeven at the operating 
PBT level. Jeevansathi reported an operating profit of Rs.2 crores and Aisle an operating loss 
of Rs.3 crores. Cash generated from operations for the segment was Rs.3 crores versus a cash 
loss of Rs.2 crores in Q2 of last year. 
 
In Jeevansathi, we retained a profile share of over 45% in Hindi-speaking markets and 
continue to lead on daily logged-in users in these markets. The team is testing a number of 
new features and paywall formats around value, convenience and affordability, and AI is 
improving recommendation quality. We expect Jeevansathi's billing growth to accelerate in 
the second half. We expect Aisle to continue on a high-growth trajectory. Since moving to a 
freemium model for women, we believe Aisle has one of the highest shares of female users 
amongst dating apps in India, which improves the experience on both sides of the platform. 
 

Lastly, the Education segment. Shiksha's billings declined 27% and revenue declined 9%. The 
business operated near breakeven at the operating PBT level, with cash losses from 
operations of Rs.16 crores. AI-driven changes in search behaviour have reduced the referral 
traffic Shiksha relied on, and this continues to affect delivery outcomes for clients. These 
changes require us to evolve the business model. That pivot is underway. We are building 
domestic counselling, supported by AI voice bots, to create a direct relationship with students 
rather than depending on search. In Study Abroad, we are widening destination coverage to 
the UK, UAE and continental Europe as student demand shifts. Our focus is on returning 
Shiksha to growth while keeping losses contained during the transition. 
 
A little on AI across InfoEdge. Let me just tell you how we are thinking about it. Beyond 
product-specific applications, AI is changing how we operate, with efficiency gains across 
functions including marketing, pricing, lead qualification, telecalling and product 
development. Across Recruitment, Real Estate and Matchmaking, our proprietary data, 
marketplace relationships and domain expertise position us to benefit from AI through better 
matching, recommendations and customer outcomes. At the same time, AI is changing how 
users discover information, and we need to keep evolving our products and business models. 
We continue to step up investment in AI infrastructure, talent and tools. In most products, AI 
improves outcomes within the core offering. Where it is sold separately, it contributes to the 
AI revenue discussed earlier. 
 
A brief word on our investment portfolio. Our investment portfolio now spans around 135 
companies across AI, deeptech and consumer tech, with about Rs.5,000 crores invested 
through our balance sheet and AIFs. Several companies have listed, and others have raised 
follow-on rounds from credible investors. We invest early and hold for the long term, and we 
expect the portfolio to create significant value for shareholders over time. 
 
Let me close with how we see the years ahead. Our strategy rests on three pillars. First, 
strengthening our core marketplaces through technology, AI and better customer outcomes. 
Second, growing our AI monetization through AI-first products, products which would not 
have existed without AI, products like AI-Rex and Talent Pulse for recruiters and AI services 
for jobseekers. Third, scaling a broader set of growth engines, including Naukri 360, Coding 
Ninjas, Job Hai, AmbitionBox, 99acres, Jeevansathi and Aisle, that expand our opportunity. 
Several have moved beyond early validation and are now scaling, with headroom from deeper 
penetration, share gains, pricing and new customer segments. As these businesses scale, 
much of the incremental revenue can be generated on our existing platforms, creating room 
for operating leverage, stronger margins and higher cash generation over time. Together, 
these give us confidence in building a more diversified and sustainable growth platform for 
the long term. 
 
Before we move to Q&A, as we announced today, I will be stepping down as Managing 
Director and CEO at the close of business on December 2nd, after nearly 27 years at InfoEdge, 
and Sanjeev will take on the role of Executive Vice Chairman, Managing Director and Group 
CEO from the 3rd of December. It has not been an easy decision, but it is one I have thought 
through carefully over time. I believe the company now has the depth of leadership and 
institutional strength to move confidently into its next phase. Subject to shareholder 
approval, I will continue on the Board as a Non-Executive Director. I would like to thank all of 
you for your trust and support over the years. With that, we are happy to take your questions. 

 
Vineet Ranjan: Thank you, Hitesh. Anand, we have a few questions already there in the 
queue. Maybe we can start with them. 
 
Anand Bansal: Thanks, Vineet. Anyone who wishes to ask a question may raise your hand. 
We have a couple of questions; we'll take them and the rest will follow one by one. The first 
question is from Sachin from Bank of America. Sachin, go ahead and ask your question. 
 
Sachin Salgaonkar: Thanks, Anand. Good day, management. I have three set of questions. 
Hitesh, your decision is surprising. Two questions out here. I just wanted to understand, will 
Sanjeev be taking over as a full-time CEO, or is it more like a stopgap arrangement till we hire 
someone new? From a transition point of view, anything we need to look at? Presume you 
will be involved in strategic decisions now that you will be a board member, subject to 
shareholder approval. 
 
Hitesh Oberoi: Sanjeev, you want to take that? 
 
Sanjeev Bikhchandani: We haven't thought about that yet. Obviously, Hitesh is still there for 
a month, and beyond that, he's there anyway and available, and I'll be taking his counsel. I'll 
be obviously talking to the NRC, and we'll figure out how to evolve the leadership structure 
at the top going forward. There's no decision taken on hiring more people yet. As far as I'm 
concerned, I'll be taking over. I'll be listening a lot. I'll be observing. I'll be asking questions. I'll 
be learning. I'll take Hitesh's guidance. The good bit is that the leadership below him, who 
work around him, is very, very good. Already I've done three meetings today in the last two 
hours, and people are totally on top of their jobs. I don't think I'll have actually that much to 
do. 
 
Sachin Salgaonkar: Got it. Thank you. Very clear. Second question, Hitesh, on the business, 
and this is largely on the billings growth in this quarter. Last quarter, we saw billings growth 
of close to around 17%, and adjusting for that one-off, let's say it was 15%. When you look at 
the revenue, typically the last quarter billing growth does translate into revenue. In that 
context, it looked a bit softer at 13%. Anything to look into that, now that the AI billings is also 
a high single digit in terms of share? Is that influencing it? Is there something out there? The 
related question is, billings growth in this quarter was 13%. Is this the new normal, or is there 
a timing issue out there where numbers could move just the way they moved last quarter? 
 
Hitesh Oberoi: Billing gets affected. A lot of our clients renew at quarter end. Sometimes 
negotiations drag. Sometimes deals close early and sales get pulled, and billing gets pulled 
into a quarter, and sometimes it gets deferred. From a billing standpoint, it's always better to 
look at YTD or at least H1, because timing differences tend to get evened out over time. In 
Q1, we actually had said on the call last time that 17.5% was not the real number. To us, it 
was more like 14-15% because some sales got pulled in. In this quarter, the timing differences 
sort of work in the other direction. Our sense is that our business is growing at 14-15% right 
now. Internally, these are the kind of targets we are setting for the sales team as well going 
forward. So that's what it looks like right now. Now, as far as revenue recognition is 
concerned, revenue is recognized over 12 months because most of our deals are annual in 
nature. Even if you renew in Q1, that deferral kicks in over the next three quarters. 
 

Sachin Salgaonkar: Got it. Directionally, revenue should be in the 14-15% range as the billings 
growth stabilizes out there. Last question I have on margins. Wanted to understand, is this 
shift towards AI-Rex directly helping in terms of margins? How to think about margins at the 
recruitment business? Clearly, for 99acres, we could see the market share change. Wanted to 
understand if this is structural, and hence, on the back of it, we should continue to see margin 
improvements at 99acres as well. 
 
Hitesh Oberoi: The AI offerings we've launched are of course very high gross margin. Our go-
to-market strategy right now, especially on the B2B side, is to go for penetration and 
adoption. We have 150,000 customers in Naukri. There are at least 40,000 large clients who 
renew annually, who buy a big product, where ARPU is high. Technically, Theoretically, it 
should be possible to sell AI-Rex to everybody, all these 40,000 accounts. Right now, the 
number of accounts who are trying AI-Rex is 2,000. Normally, when clients start with a new 
product, they start small. They try it out. If they're happy, they renew, they buy more. On the 
AI-Rex front, our strategy is to make it like a no-brainer for clients who try it out, because we 
are very confident of the product and our ability to deliver. Our goal for the next, I would say, 
maybe 24 months is going to be to drive penetration, to get as many customers to use AI-Rex 
as possible, and then to get them to adopt it, use it and then renew, and at renewal time, get 
them to upgrade and buy more. In the end, we believe that customers who move to AI-Rex 
will end up hiring more people through Naukri. Our hiring share will grow with them. They 
will also be able to hire talent faster and better, and their recruiters will become more 
productive. Ultimately, this will mean more revenue for us and higher growth for us, and at 
high margins, because once the technology is developed, once the Capex is done, there's not 
much incremental cost. That's our philosophy. This is the approach we followed with Resdex 
maybe 25 years ago when we launched Resdex. Today, a large percentage of our revenue 
comes from Resdex. 70-80% of our revenue in Naukri comes from Resdex. In the early years, 
we gave Resdex for free. Then we made it half price. Then after that also, we gave a lot of 
discounts. If you look at where we are today, we perhaps charge maybe 5x or 10x of what we 
used to charge back then. Because once the product starts to work, once customers get 
hooked, once it starts to deliver, once they start making a lot of hiring through it, then it's 
easy to realize value. That's the approach we're taking for both AI-Rex and Talent Pulse. 
 
On the jobseeker side, our AI offerings are doing really well. AI is allowing us to price them 
cheap. AI is allowing us to launch new products which could not have been possible without 
AI, like interview prep. We've launched a jobseeker agent, Neo. These products will keep 
improving. But already, if you look at what has happened over the last five or six quarters, 
jobseeker penetration of paid products has moved from maybe 1.5% to 2.6-2.7% of monthly 
active users on Naukri. We see a huge opportunity here. There are many more products which 
are under development. We have a huge product pipeline as well, both on the jobseeker and 
on the recruiter side. We feel confident about this strategy. We are going to keep pushing in 
this direction. Our hope and our core belief is that if, in the end, more people get hired 
through Naukri, if our hiring share continues to increase, revenue growth will follow. Business 
models may keep evolving, will keep evolving. 
 
Sachin Salgaonkar: Very clear, Hitesh. Any number in terms of where steady-state margins 
could be in case of the new normal, where AI-Rex becomes a larger part of the product? 
 

Hitesh Oberoi: I don't know. It'll depend on what our hiring share ultimately ends up being. If 
today 40% of all people are hired through Naukri, if that number goes to 60% over time, who 
the knows where margins will go? Margins are not really our focus right now. It's about getting 
more sales, it's about getting more users, more clients, it's about getting adoption going. 
Inherently, the product is high gross margin. If you are able to sell and if you are able to 
upgrade clients. Like last quarter, we did notice that clients who bought our AI offerings ended 
up paying us on the average at least 10 to 15% more than clients who did not buy AI offerings. 
We were able to get higher upgrades. Clients also want to try these out, and hopefully they'll 
work. I don't think margins will go down. Margins will only improve if we are successful. But 
we have to ensure that sales keep growing at higher than 10% year on year. 
 
Similarly, your other question was around 99acres. There we've been highlighting for the last 
seven, eight quarters now that we've been gaining traffic share, and revenue share follows 
with a lag. That's how it's playing out. Our business grew by 21% last quarter. In fact, 
September growth was even higher. In almost every city now, we are clear leaders. Our 
revenue market share, according to us, in our core categories, is now hitting 50%, and we 
continue to gain share. Our sense is that our competition, in both cases, their revenue actually 
declined last quarter. That's what we're hearing from the market. We continue to get stronger 
and stronger. Like any marketplace business, this is a network effect business; there's a 
flywheel. If you get strong, if you start gaining share, it's very hard for others to catch up. At 
the same time, because of what has happened in our category, the competitive intensity has 
gone down. Housing, which was owned by REA earlier, has sold their business to Aurum, and 
Aurum has gone on record saying that they want to break even over the next four to five 
quarters. This means lower marketing cost. We are under no pressure to spend more on 
marketing. Platform is built, operating leverage is playing out, 99acres generated Rs.20 
crores+ cash this quarter. If we continue to execute like this, things will only get better. 
 
Sachin Salgaonkar: Thank you. Very clear. 
 
Anand Bansal: Thanks, Sachin. Next question is from Vijit Jain from Citi. Vijit, go ahead and 
ask your question. 
 
Vijit Jain: Thank you so much for the opportunity. Hitesh, again, I'll echo what Sachin said 
earlier; it came as a bit of a surprise. My question is, if my understanding is right, property 
and other segments have CBO positions already. I know Pawan left the platform a few months 
back. Is that the structure that you would again seek to go back to for the recruitment 
business as well? If my understanding is right, there is no CBO at the moment there. 
 
Hitesh Oberoi: Like Sanjeev said earlier, he's going to take over as Group CEO, and he's going 
to meet everybody and then slowly make up his mind on what next. For the longest time, I 
believe now that we have a crack team in all our verticals. We have people who've been 
around for several years. They have grown with the business. They have matured as leaders. 
We have a crack team in Naukri. We have solid leadership in Job Hai, 99acres, Jeevansathi. 
That actually gave me the confidence to move on. I guess what you're saying, and I guess 
Sanjeev will sort of take over and then. 
 
Sanjeev Bikhchandani: I think nothing in a hurry. The first priority will be to give internal 
people an opportunity to grow. Then we'll take a look. Like I said, I'll listen to Hitesh a lot. He 

is there, is around, is available even after December 2. I'll listen to the NRC a lot. I'll listen to 
the current people inside the company a lot, and then we'll figure it out. 
 
Vijit Jain: Understood. Thank you, Sanjeev. Appreciate that. My second question, good to see 
the AI billings disclosure. Wanted to understand the ARR a little bit. Suffice to say that the 
ARR, the Rs.2.4 billion, is higher than what you would have seen in 2Q, right? So just wanted 
to get a sense of the pace of growth we are looking at there. Second, should we think of this 
as additive versus last year or is there an element of the nature of deals changing as well 
there? 
 
Hitesh Oberoi: There was some AI revenue last year as well. We did not report it separately, 
especially on the jobseeker side. Talent Pulse was there last year as well, so there was some 
revenue from Talent Pulse. AI-Rex is new. We got only a little revenue from AI-Rex in Q1, but 
it scaled up massively in Q2. When I say ARR is Rs.240 crores, what we really mean is Q2 
revenue into four is what we see as ARR. Q2 revenue from AI-first products and services, 
products which could not have been possible to launch without AI, was around Rs.60 crores. 
That's what we mean by it. 
 
Sanjeev Bikhchandani: Not as if it's cannibalizing existing revenue. 
 
Vijit Jain: So, this is nearly all additive, and there would have been a non-zero number in the 
base but mostly coming from Talent Pulse. Understood. Perfect. Thank you so much. 
 
Hitesh Oberoi: And jobseeker services. There were some jobseeker services which had been 
launched by Q2 of last year. 
 
Vijit Jain: Understood. A related question to that, and this is more an in-principal question. In 
general, do you think that bundled pricing is the way AI and AI offerings would seep through 
into your billings and revenue overall? By that, I mean is you don't necessarily charge for each 
individual AI product, but your clients use them, and it enables you to raise your pricing over 
time. Is that the right way to think about pricing, a bundled approach versus a disaggregated 
approach? 
 
Hitesh Oberoi: No, right now, we are pricing them separately. We have a price for AI-Rex per 
mandate: Rs.3,500 per mandate for companies, Rs.2,500 for consultants. That was the other 
big thing, we rolled out AI-Rex for consultants also in Q2. We had not rolled it out for 
consultants in Q1. There's a rate card rate. Similarly, there's a rate card rate for Talent Pulse. 
But often, when we sell to clients, they buy multiple products at the same time, and then 
there's a negotiation. They may buy Resdex, they buy job listings, they may buy AmbitionBox, 
they may buy AI-Rex, they may buy Talent Pulse, and there's a negotiation. In that sense, 
when it is sold, it is sold as a bundle, but there is a separate rate card for Talent Pulse. 
 
Vijit Jain: Understood. Perfect. Thank you. My last question, on advertisement spends, just 
on the B2C side. Given that is growing very strongly, 37% this year YoY, I'm wondering, with 
AI-powered offerings there and all the growth you're seeing there, and given where the 
market dynamics are, does it warrant higher ad spends, maybe targeted more towards 
candidates, which highlights some of these things? Or it's not necessary because candidates 
come to your platform anyway? 

 
Hitesh Oberoi: Like I said, we are selling paid services to 2.7% of all our monthly active users 
on Naukri right now. There are a whole bunch of users still left to sell something to. This 
number was 1.5% one year, maybe four, five, six quarters ago. There's ample room to sell AI 
services and our AI offerings to more jobseekers on Naukri. We don't need to advertise for 
this purpose. We may want to advertise because we want more jobseekers on the platform. 
We want to grow our share amongst jobseekers, etc. That's a different reason, but not to sell 
these services. 
 
Vijit Jain: Understood. Thank you so much and again, best of luck to you, Hitesh, and to 
everyone else. I look forward to seeing you guys soon again. 
 
Anand Bansal: Thank you, Vijit. The next question is from Vivek from Ambit Capital. Vivek, go 
ahead and ask your question. 
 
Vivekanand Subbaraman: Thanks for taking my call. Hitesh and Sanjeev, just a couple of 
questions on your transition. In the last one year, we've seen Chintan and Pawan go. Was it 
really necessary for you to step down at this juncture, given that the CBO role is also vacant? 
How are you thinking about filling these leadership roles? I heard Sanjeev's answer that 
internal succession is what he'll prioritize, but in terms of org structure, any thoughts that will 
help? A related question, Hitesh, for you. Now, as co-promoter, you still have 5% stake in the
